title: Designer supervision: what it is and why you need it during a renovation
seo_title: Design Supervision During Renovation: Why It Matters
description: Designer supervision during a renovation: what it includes, when it is needed, how it saves budget and helps you get the interior you saw in the 3D visualisation.
lead: Even a perfect design can be ruined on the building site. Designer supervision (author's supervision) is control over the renovation so that it follows the design and the finished interior looks exactly like the 3D visualisation.
photo_alt: Beige living room with an open kitchen, a light sofa and a marble splashback — Edelweiss design project
body: h2
What designer supervision is
p

A design project consists of drawings, wall elevations, lighting and socket plans, and specifications for materials and furniture. But drawings do not build themselves: the crew reads them, and every tradesperson may interpret a detail in their own way. Designer supervision means the author of the design takes part in the renovation: the designer visits the site, checks that everything is built to the drawings and resolves questions that arise during the works.
p

It is not the same as technical supervision or a site manager's job. The site manager is responsible for organising the works and the quality of execution; the designer is responsible for the result matching the intent: proportions, heights, lines of light, material junctions, colours.
p

Supervision is not only about a beautiful result. It is often on site that you discover a wall differs from the survey, a riser runs somewhere unexpected or the chosen material has been discontinued. In such cases the decision should be made by the author of the design, who understands how the change will affect the rest of the interior.
h2
What designer supervision includes
ul
site visits at key stages
checking compliance with the drawings: walls, sockets, lighting, plumbing
answering the crew's questions
adjusting decisions if site conditions require it
approving material substitutions
checking measurements for bespoke furniture before it is made
overseeing final installation: light fittings, doors, cabinet fronts, decor

h2
When supervision is especially important
ul
complex solutions: concealed doors, niches, lighting details, marble and large-format tiles
bespoke furniture that has to fit niches precisely
the renovation is done by a third-party crew
you cannot visit the site often — for example, you live abroad
the design has many non-standard details and junctions of different materials
p
In a simple cosmetic renovation supervision can be minimal. But the more concealed and precise details the design has, the more important it is that they are checked by the person who designed them.
h2
How designer supervision saves money
p
A mistake spotted before it is covered with tiles or plasterboard is cheap to fix. Afterwards it costs several times more. Supervision pays for itself with the first detail it saves.
p

Money is most often lost not on big decisions but on small things: a socket ends up behind a wardrobe, a tap outlet is at the wrong height, a TV niche is narrower than needed, the LED strip does not fit its groove. Each of these means demolition, new materials and a shifted schedule. A designer on site catches them during rough works, when the fix takes minutes rather than days.
p

Purchasing is another source of savings. When the designer approves substitutions, you do not overpay for materials that turn out to be the wrong size or shade, and you do not buy extra just in case. It is simplest of all when [turnkey procurement](/en/turnkey-procurement) is run by the same team that did the design.
h2
At which stages the designer visits the site
ol
after partitions are set out — checking the layout and openings
after electrical and plumbing first fix — sockets, switches, outlets
before screed and ceilings — levels, niches, lighting recesses
before tiling — tile layout, starting lines, cuts
before ordering furniture — final measurements of niches and openings
during final installation — lighting, cabinet fronts, doors, decor
p
The exact visit schedule depends on the complexity of the property and is agreed in the contract.

h2
Typical mistakes without designer supervision
ul
the crew simplifies a complex detail, and the intended line or shadow gap disappears
a material is replaced with the same but cheaper one in a different shade or texture
furniture is ordered to drawing dimensions without checking the real walls
light fittings are installed off-plan, and lighting scenes do not work
the crew's questions are answered by whoever is nearby, not by the author of the design
h2
Checklist: how to organise designer supervision
ul
set out in the contract the number of visits and the stages that need them
agree on a communication channel between designer and crew
record every change and substitution in writing or in photo reports
give the crew the full set of drawings before works start
approve any material substitution with the designer before purchasing
p
Well-organised supervision does not slow the renovation down — on the contrary, the crew spends less time waiting for answers, and decisions are made on the spot.

faq: How many times does the designer visit the site?
It depends on the stages and complexity; the visit schedule is agreed in the contract.
You can, but the risk that the result will differ from the 3D visualisation is higher.
How does designer supervision differ from technical supervision?
Technical supervision checks the quality and methods of the works; designer supervision checks that the result matches the design: dimensions, materials, lighting, details.
Can I order designer supervision if my own crew does the renovation?
Yes, designer supervision can be ordered separately — the designer will work with your crew from the project drawings.
